````
  content: |
      #!/usr/bin/env bash
      # ai-rss — start the full local stack (all offline-capable once models are cached)
      #
      #   ./start.sh           start everything
      #   ./start.sh status    show what's running
      #   ./start.sh stop      stop everything
      #   ./start.sh video     render a test video right now
      #   ./start.sh smoke     full end-to-end test through n8n's webhook
      #
      # Services:
      #   llama-server    :1234   LLM that writes the script (Llama 3.2 3B, local GGUF)
      #   comfyui         :8188   SD-Turbo AI backgrounds (CPU)
      #   voicebox        :17493  kokoro TTS voiceover (CPU)
      #   ai-rss-render   :8777   render bridge n8n talks to
      #   n8n             :5678   workflow orchestrator (docker compose)
      
      set -u
      
      UNITS=(llama-server comfyui voicebox ai-rss-render)
      N8N_DIR="$HOME/docker/n8n"
      
      is_up() { curl -s --max-time 3 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' "$1" 2>/dev/null | grep -q 200; }
      
      wait_for() { # wait_for <name> <url> <tries>
        local name="$1" url="$2" tries="${3:-30}"
        for _ in $(seq 1 "$tries"); do
          is_up "$url" && { echo "  ✓ $name is up ($url)"; return 0; }
          sleep 2
        done
        echo "  ✗ $name did not come up at $url" >&2
        return 1
      }
      
      start() {
        echo "Starting ai-rss stack..."
        for u in "${UNITS[@]}"; do
          systemctl --user enable --now "$u.service" >/dev/null 2>&1
          systemctl --user start "$u.service" 2>/dev/null
        done
        if docker compose -f "$N8N_DIR/docker-compose.yml" ps -q n8n 2>/dev/null | grep -q .; then
          echo "  ✓ n8n container already running"
        else
          (cd "$N8N_DIR" && docker compose up -d) >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo "  ✓ n8n container started"
        fi
        wait_for "llama-server"  "http://127.0.0.1:1234/health"
        wait_for "comfyui"       "http://127.0.0.1:8188/system_stats"
        wait_for "voicebox"      "http://127.0.0.1:17493/health"
        wait_for "render server" "http://127.0.0.1:8777/health"
        wait_for "n8n"           "http://localhost:5678/healthz"
        echo ""
        echo "Stack ready."
        echo "  - Render a video now:   ./start.sh video"
        echo "  - Full webhook test:    ./start.sh smoke"
        echo "  - Daily schedule:       n8n fires automatically at 9:00 AM"
      }
      
      stop() {
        echo "Stopping ai-rss stack..."
        for u in "${UNITS[@]}"; do systemctl --user stop "$u.service" 2>/dev/null; done
        (cd "$N8N_DIR" && docker compose stop) >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo "  ✓ all stopped"
      }
      
      status() {
        printf "%-14s %-8s %s\n" "SERVICE" "STATE" "ENDPOINT"
        for u in "${UNITS[@]}"; do
          printf "%-14s %-8s %s\n" "$u" "$(systemctl --user is-active "$u.service" 2>/dev/null || echo '?')"
        done
        printf "%-14s %-8s %s\n" "n8n" "$(docker compose -f "$N8N_DIR/docker-compose.yml" ps n8n 2>/dev/null | grep -q n8n && echo active || echo inactive)" "http://localhost:5678"
        echo ""
        is_up "http://127.0.0.1:1234/health"          && echo "  ✓ LLM responding"
        is_up "http://127.0.0.1:8188/system_stats"    && echo "  ✓ ComfyUI responding"
        is_up "http://127.0.0.1:17493/health"         && echo "  ✓ voicebox responding"
        is_up "http://127.0.0.1:8777/health"          && echo "  ✓ render server responding"
      }
      
      video() {
        echo "Rendering a video via the render server (LLM-free manual script)..."
        curl -s --max-time 560 -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8777/render \
          -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
          -d '{
            "title": "Manual Test Video",
            "segments": [
              "Spuds, this is a manual render straight from start.sh.",
              "Voiceover comes from kokoro, background from SD-Turbo, all on your CPU.",
              "Drop a comment if this is crisp enough. This is Potaterrr - stay crispy."
            ]
          }'
        echo
      }
      
      smoke() {
        echo "Firing n8n smoke webhook (full daily path minus the LLM)..."
        curl -s --max-time 560 -X POST http://localhost:5678/webhook/ai-rss/smoke \
          -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{}'
        echo
      }
      
      case "${1:-start}" in
        start)  start ;;
        stop)   stop ;;
        status) status ;;
        video)  video ;;
        smoke)  smoke ;;
        *) echo "usage: $0 {start|stop|status|video|smoke}"; exit 1 ;;
      esac

- path: readme.md
  content: |
      # AI-RSS — Python News Video Generator
      
      An n8n pipeline that turns **Hacker News Python stories** into a **Linus-Tech-Tips-style news video** — AI-generated background, voiceover, burned-in subtitles — saved to `~/Downloads/generated` and pushed to Telegram.
      
      ```
      HN Python feed (daily 9AM) → local LLM writes the script (your prompt)
        → voicebox TTS voiceover → ComfyUI (SD-Turbo) AI background
        → ffmpeg renders 1080x1920 MP4 with subtitles
        → saved to ~/Downloads/generated → Telegram sendVideo
      ```
      
      ## 🧩 Architecture
      
      ```
      ┌─────────────── Docker (~/docker/n8n) ───────────────┐
      │  n8n  →  Schedule 9AM + Webhook /ai-rss/smoke       │
      │          HTTP nodes call the render server          │
      └──────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────┘
                             │ POST http://host.docker.internal:8777/render
      ┌──────────────────────▼───────────── Host ───────────┐
      │  render_server.py (systemd: ai-rss-render)          │
      │    1. voicebox_tts.py    → TTS voiceover (MP3)      │
      │    2. comfy_bg.py        → SD-Turbo 1080x1920 PNG   │
      │       (via ComfyUI API on :8188, --cpu)             │
      │    3. render_video.py    → ffmpeg + ASS subtitles   │
      │    4. notify_telegram.py → sendVideo + caption      │
      │  Output: ~/Downloads/generated/                     │
      └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
      ```
      
      Everything render-side is **stdlib-only Python** — no pip deps on the host.
      Failures degrade gracefully: no voicebox → silent video, no ComfyUI → gradient background, no Telegram → skipped.
      
      ## 📥 Setup
      
      ### 1. Services (all systemd user units, auto-start on boot)
      - **n8n**: `~/docker/n8n` compose, custom image `n8n-with-renderer` (n8n + static python3 + ffmpeg, repo mounted at `/data/ai-rss`, output at `/data/generated`).
      - **Render server**: `ai-rss-render.service` — HTTP bridge on :8777 (n8n calls this).
      - **ComfyUI**: `comfyui.service` — `--cpu`, :8188, model `sd_turbo.safetensors`.
      - **voicebox**: `voicebox.service` — :17493, engine kokoro (CPU-friendly), profile `potaterrr` (voice `af_bella`).
      - **llama-server**: `llama-server.service` — llama.cpp on :1234, `Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct-Q4_K_M` (local GGUF in `~/git-clones/llama.cpp/models/`).
      
      Everything is **fully offline** once models are cached (they are). Control it all with:
      ```bash
      ./start.sh          # start the whole stack + wait until healthy
      ./start.sh status   # what's running
      ./start.sh video    # render a video right now (manual script)
      ./start.sh smoke    # fire the n8n smoke webhook
      ./start.sh stop     # stop everything
      ```
      
      All three units live in this repo and are installed to `~/.config/systemd/user/` (linger enabled).
      
      ```bash
      systemctl --user status ai-rss-render comfyui voicebox
      curl localhost:8188/system_stats           # ComfyUI
      curl localhost:17493/health                # voicebox
      ```
      
      voicebox first-time setup (one-off, already done): Python **3.12** venv via uv (kokoro needs <3.13), CPU torch, `backend/requirements.txt`, then `chatterbox-tts`/`hume-tada` with `--no-deps`. The `potaterrr` voice profile (kokoro/af_bella) already exists.
      
      llama.cpp first-time setup (one-off, already done): model GGUF lives in `~/git-clones/llama.cpp/models/`; unit runs `llama-server --port 1234 --ctx-size 8192 --threads 6`.
      
      ### 2. n8n workflow
      Imported via API as **"AI-RSS - Python News Video Generator"** (id `22p8GqfGEC4myY9d`). `workflow.json` + `build_workflow.py` in this repo are the source of truth — edit `build_workflow.py`, re-run it, then re-import.
      
      ### 3. Telegram
      Create a bot with @BotFather → put the real values in `~/docker/n8n/.env`:
      ```
      TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN=123456:ABC...
      TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID=your_numeric_id
      ```
      then `cd ~/docker/n8n && docker compose up -d`. (Get your chat id from @userinfobot.)
      
      ### 4. ⚠️ Firewall (need sudo, already applied for :8777)
      n8n runs in Docker; ufw blocks container→host traffic. Ports the container must reach on the host:
      ```bash
      sudo ufw allow from 172.16.0.0/12 to any port 8777 proto tcp   # render server (done)
      sudo ufw allow from 172.16.0.0/12 to any port 1234 proto tcp   # llama-server (pending)
      ```
      
      ## 🔥 Smoke test
      
      ```bash
      curl -X POST http://localhost:5678/webhook/ai-rss/smoke \
        -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{}'
      ```
      
      No LLM/TTS/ComfyUI needed. Expected response:
      ```json
      {"status": "ok", "smoke": true, "video_path": ".../ai_rss_....mp4",
       "voice": "skipped", "background": "gradient", "telegram": "sent|skipped"}
      ```
      
      Host-side test (bypasses n8n entirely):
      ```bash
      curl -X POST http://localhost:8777/render -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
        -d '{"title":"T","segments":["Hello.","Second line."],"smoke":true}'
      ```
      
      ## ✍️ Your prompt
      
      Edit `SYSTEM_PROMPT` in `build_workflow.py` (marker: `<<ADD YOUR PERSONAL PROMPT / CHANNEL STYLE HERE>>`), re-run it, re-import. Or edit the **Write Script (Local LLM)** node directly in n8n.
      
      ## 📁 Files
      
      | File | Role |
      |---|---|
      | `workflow.json` | n8n workflow (generated) |
      | `build_workflow.py` | Generates `workflow.json` — edit prompts/nodes here |
      | `render_server.py` | HTTP bridge :8777 — orchestrates the render chain |
      | `render_video.py` | ffmpeg renderer — ASS subtitles, title card, background |
      | `comfy_bg.py` | ComfyUI client — SD-Turbo vertical background |
      | `voicebox_tts.py` | voicebox client — submit/poll/download MP3 |
      | `notify_telegram.py` | Telegram notifier — message + sendVideo |
      | `ai-rss-render.service` | systemd user unit — render server |
      | `comfyui.service` | systemd user unit — ComfyUI |
      | `voicebox.service` | systemd user unit — voicebox TTS |
      | `llama-server.service` | systemd user unit — llama.cpp LLM |
      | `start.sh` | one-command control for the whole stack |
      | `out/` | gitignored artifacts |
````

````
- path: render_server.py
  content: |
      #!/usr/bin/env python3
      """Local render server for ai-rss — the bridge between n8n and the render pipeline.
      
      n8n (in Docker) calls POST http://host.docker.internal:8777/render with:
        {"title": "...", "segments": ["...", ...], "smoke": false}
      
      The server runs, in order:
        1. voicebox TTS        (skipped when smoke=true, non-fatal on failure)
        2. ComfyUI AI background (skipped when smoke=true, non-fatal on failure)
        3. ffmpeg render with subtitles
        4. Telegram notify with the video attached (skipped when not configured)
      
      Response: {"video_path": ..., "voice": ok|failed|skipped, "background": comfy|gradient,
                 "telegram": sent|skipped|failed:..., "title": ...}
      
      Stdlib-only. Run: RENDER_SERVER_PORT=8777 python3 render_server.py
      """
      import json
      import os
      import subprocess
      import sys
      import tempfile
      from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer
      from pathlib import Path
      
      RENDER_DIR = Path(os.environ.get("RENDER_DIR", str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent)))
      OUT_DIR = Path(os.environ.get("OUTPUT_DIR", str(RENDER_DIR / "out"))).expanduser()
      # If OUTPUT_DIR exists but isn't writable (e.g. root-owned from Docker auto-create),
      # degrade to a user-writable fallback instead of failing every render.
      if OUT_DIR.exists() and not os.access(OUT_DIR, os.W_OK):
          FALLBACK_DIR = Path.home() / ".cache" / "ai-rss" / "generated"
          OUT_DIR = FALLBACK_DIR
      else:
          FALLBACK_DIR = None
      PORT = int(os.environ.get("RENDER_SERVER_PORT", "8777"))
      
      PY = sys.executable
      
      
      def run(cmd: list[str], timeout: int, env: dict | None = None) -> tuple[int, str, str]:
          p = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout, env=env)
          return p.returncode, p.stdout, p.stderr
      
      
      def run_with_env(cmd: list[str], timeout: int, env: dict) -> tuple[int, str, str]:
          return run(cmd, timeout, env=env)
      
      
      class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
          def log_message(self, *args):  # quiet
              pass
      
          def _json(self, code: int, obj: dict) -> None:
              body = json.dumps(obj).encode()
              self.send_response(code)
              self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
              self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
              self.end_headers()
              self.wfile.write(body)
      
          def do_GET(self):
              if self.path == "/health":
                  self._json(200, {"status": "ok"})
              else:
                  self._json(404, {"error": "not found"})
      
          def do_POST(self):
              if self.path != "/render":
                  self._json(404, {"error": "not found"})
                  return
              try:
                  n = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length", 0))
                  req = json.loads(self.rfile.read(n) or b"{}")
              except Exception as e:
                  self._json(400, {"error": f"bad json: {e}"})
                  return
      
              title = str(req.get("title", "Python News"))[:80]
              segments = [str(s).strip() for s in req.get("segments", []) if str(s).strip()]
              smoke = bool(req.get("smoke"))
              if not segments:
                  self._json(400, {"error": "no segments"})
                  return
      
              result = {
                  "title": title,
                  "voice": "skipped" if smoke else "failed",
                  "background": "gradient",
                  "telegram": "skipped",
              }
      
              tmpdir = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="ai_rss_")
              payload_path = os.path.join(tmpdir, "payload.json")
              with open(payload_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                  json.dump({"title": title, "segments": segments}, f, ensure_ascii=False)
      
              # 1. voicebox TTS (non-fatal)
              voice_path = ""
              if not smoke:
                  voice_path = os.path.join(tmpdir, "voice.mp3")
                  try:
                      rc, out, err = run(
                          [PY, str(RENDER_DIR / "voicebox_tts.py"), voice_path, "--payload", payload_path],
                          960,
                      )
                      result["voice"] = "ok" if (rc == 0 and "VOICE=ok" in out) else "failed"
                      if result["voice"] == "failed":
                          voice_path = ""
                          result["voice_detail"] = (out or err).strip().splitlines()[-1][:200] if (out or err).strip() else "unknown"
                  except Exception as e:
                      result["voice"] = "failed"
                      result["voice_detail"] = str(e)[:200]
                      voice_path = ""
      
              # 2. ComfyUI AI background is handled inside render_video.py via AI_RSS_COMFY=1
              #    (smoke renders force the gradient so they stay fast and dependency-free)
              result["background"] = "comfy" if (os.environ.get("AI_RSS_COMFY") == "1" and not smoke) else "gradient"
              render_env = dict(os.environ)
              if smoke:
                  render_env["AI_RSS_COMFY"] = "0"
      
              # 3. Render
              cmd = [PY, str(RENDER_DIR / "render_video.py"), payload_path, "--out", str(OUT_DIR)]
              if voice_path and os.path.isfile(voice_path):
                  cmd += ["--voice", voice_path]
              try:
                  rc, out, err = run_with_env(cmd, 1800, render_env)
              except Exception as e:
                  self._json(500, {"error": f"render crashed: {e}", **result})
                  return
              if rc != 0:
                  self._json(500, {"error": ((err or out) or "renderer failed")[-800:], **result})
                  return
      
              video = ""
              for line in out.splitlines():
                  if line.startswith("VIDEO_PATH="):
                      video = line.split("=", 1)[1].strip()
              if not video:
                  self._json(500, {"error": "no VIDEO_PATH in renderer output", "stdout": out[-400:], **result})
                  return
              result["video_path"] = video
              if FALLBACK_DIR:
                  result["warning"] = (
                      f"OUTPUT_DIR not writable — video saved to {FALLBACK_DIR}. "
                      "Fix: sudo chown $USER:$USER ~/Downloads/generated"
                  )
      
              # 4. Telegram (non-fatal, skipped when unconfigured)
              try:
                  rc, tout, terr = run(
                      [PY, str(RENDER_DIR / "notify_telegram.py"),
                       "--text", f"✅ {title} — new Python news video ready",
                       "--video", video],
                      360,
                  )
                  if rc == 0:
                      result["telegram"] = "sent" if "message sent" not in tout and "skipping" not in tout else "skipped"
                      if "video sent" in tout:
                          result["telegram"] = "sent"
                      elif "skipping" in tout or "not configured" in tout:
                          result["telegram"] = "skipped"
                  else:
                      result["telegram"] = f"failed: {(terr or tout).strip()[-200:]}"
              except Exception as e:
                  result["telegram"] = f"failed: {str(e)[:200]}"
      
              self._json(200, result)
      
      
      if __name__ == "__main__":
          OUT_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
          # 0.0.0.0 so the n8n container can reach it via host.docker.internal
          print(f"ai-rss render server on 0.0.0.0:{PORT} | out={OUT_DIR} | comfy={os.environ.get('AI_RSS_COMFY', '0')}")
          ThreadingHTTPServer(("0.0.0.0", PORT), Handler).serve_forever()

- path: voicebox_tts.py
  content: |
      #!/usr/bin/env python3
      """Generate a voiceover MP3 via a local voicebox server and save it to disk.
      
      voicebox exposes an async job API:
        POST /speak  -> {"id": ...}  (status "generating")
        GET  /generate/{id}/status -> poll until done
        GET  /audio/{id}           -> the audio file
      
      Usage: voicebox_tts.py <out.mp3> --payload payload.json
      Env: VOICEBOX_BASE_URL (default http://127.0.0.1:17493)
           VOICEBOX_PROFILE  (voice profile name; empty = server default)
           VOICEBOX_ENGINE   (default kokoro — the CPU-friendly engine)
      
      Never hard-fails the pipeline: prints VOICE=ok or VOICE=failed and exits 0,
      so the caller can render a silent video when voicebox is unavailable.
      Stdlib-only.
      """
      import argparse
      import json
      import os
      import sys
      import time
      import urllib.request
      
      BASE = os.environ.get("VOICEBOX_BASE_URL", "http://127.0.0.1:17493").rstrip("/")
      PROFILE = os.environ.get("VOICEBOX_PROFILE", "potaterrr") or None
      ENGINE = os.environ.get("VOICEBOX_ENGINE", "kokoro")
      
      DONE_STATES = {"completed", "complete", "success", "done"}
      FAIL_STATES = {"failed", "error", "cancelled", "canceled"}
      
      
      def request_json(url: str, payload: dict | None = None, timeout: int = 30) -> dict:
          data = json.dumps(payload).encode() if payload is not None else None
          req = urllib.request.Request(
              url, data=data, headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"} if data else {}
          )
          with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=timeout) as resp:
              body = resp.read().decode("utf-8", errors="replace").strip()
          # /status returns SSE ("data: {...}" lines) — extract the last JSON payload.
          if body.startswith("data:"):
              for line in reversed(body.splitlines()):
                  line = line.strip()
                  if line.startswith("data:"):
                      chunk = line[5:].strip()
                      if chunk and chunk != "[DONE]":
                          return json.loads(chunk)
              return {}
          return json.loads(body) if body else {}
      
      
      def main() -> None:
          ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Voicebox TTS for ai-rss")
          ap.add_argument("out", help="output mp3 path")
          ap.add_argument("--payload", required=True, help="ai-rss payload JSON with title+segments")
          args = ap.parse_args()
      
          try:
              payload = json.loads(open(args.payload, encoding="utf-8").read())
              text = "\n\n".join(str(s) for s in payload.get("segments", []) if str(s).strip())
              if not text:
                  raise ValueError("payload has no segments")
          except Exception as e:
              print(f"VOICE=failed reason=bad_payload ({e})")
              sys.exit(0)
      
          body = {"text": text}
          if PROFILE:
              body["profile"] = PROFILE
          if ENGINE:
              body["engine"] = ENGINE
      
          # 1. Submit the speak job.
          try:
              resp = request_json(f"{BASE}/speak", body, timeout=30)
              gen_id = resp.get("id")
              if not gen_id:
                  raise ValueError(f"no job id in response: {str(resp)[:200]}")
          except Exception as e:
              print(f"VOICE=failed reason=speak_submit ({e})")
              sys.exit(0)
      
          # 2. Poll status (voicebox renders on CPU first run may load models — be patient).
          deadline = time.time() + 900
          final = None
          while time.time() < deadline:
              try:
                  status = request_json(f"{BASE}/generate/{gen_id}/status", timeout=15)
                  state = str(status.get("status", "")).lower()
                  if state in DONE_STATES:
                      final = gen_id
                      break
                  if state in FAIL_STATES:
                      print(f"VOICE=failed reason=job_{state} detail={str(status)[:200]}")
                      sys.exit(0)
              except Exception:
                  pass  # transient network hiccup — keep polling
              time.sleep(3)
      
          if final is None:
              print("VOICE=failed reason=timeout")
              sys.exit(0)
      
          # 3. Download the audio.
          try:
              req = urllib.request.Request(f"{BASE}/audio/{final}")
              with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=120) as r:
                  data = r.read()
              with open(args.out, "wb") as f:
                  f.write(data)
              print(f"VOICE=ok path={args.out} bytes={len(data)}")
          except Exception as e:

      #!/usr/bin/env python3
      """Builds workflow.json for the ai-rss pipeline. Run: python3 build_workflow.py"""
      import json
      from pathlib import Path
      
      PROMPT_MARKER = "<<ADD YOUR PERSONAL PROMPT / CHANNEL STYLE HERE>>"
      
      SYSTEM_PROMPT = (
          "You are the ghostwriter for 'Potaterrr', a tech & AI news channel. You receive a raw "
          "digest of today's Python/tech stories and turn it into ONE short video script. "
          "You are a writer, NOT a link aggregator. RULES: "
          "1. For EACH story write ONE spoken segment, max 2 sentences, plain friendly language a "
          "non-technical viewer understands. Explain why it matters, don't describe the headline back. "
          "2. NEVER include URLs or mention links - they are for your reference only. If an item can't "
          "be summarized without its link, skip it. "
          "3. Keep the whole script tight: 6 to 12 segments, each under 30 words, each readable aloud "
          "as one flowing line. "
          "4. Voice: playful but informative, confident, occasional light humor. Refer to the audience "
          "as 'spuds' occasionally. Have fun, but never at the expense of clarity. "
          "5. Structure: segment 1 is a catchy hook (max 12 words, no hashtags); middle segments are "
          "one per story with a headline YOU rewrote yourself (never copied) plus your summary; the "
          "final segment is a call to engage (a question or 'drop a comment') ending with the sign-off "
          "'This is Potaterrr - stay crispy, spuds.' "
          "6. Plain text only: no hashtags, no markdown, no URLs, no emoji (this is read aloud by TTS). "
          "STYLE NOTES (edit me): " + PROMPT_MARKER + " "
          'Respond with ONLY minified JSON, no markdown fences: {"title": "max 60 chars", '
          '"segments": ["sentence", ...]}'
      )
      
      DIGEST_JS = """// Flatten the parsed RSS feed into a clean story digest.
      const channel = $json.rss && $json.rss.channel ? $json.rss.channel : {};
      let rawItems = channel.item || [];
      if (!Array.isArray(rawItems)) rawItems = [rawItems];
      const text = (v) => {
        if (v == null) return '';
        if (typeof v === 'object') v = v['#text'] || v._ || v.$t || '';
        return String(v).replace(/<[^>]+>/g, ' ').replace(/&\\w+;/g, ' ').replace(/\\s+/g, ' ').trim();
      };
      const seen = new Set();
      const stories = [];
      for (const it of rawItems) {
        const title = text(it.title);
        const link = text(it.link);
        if (!title || !link) continue;
        const id = text(it.guid) || link;
        if (seen.has(id)) continue;
        seen.add(id);
        stories.push({ title, link, snippet: text(it.description).slice(0, 320) });
      }
      stories.length = Math.min(stories.length, 10);
      if (!stories.length) throw new Error('No stories found in the feed.');
      const digest = stories.map((s, i) => `${i + 1}. ${s.title} - ${s.snippet || '(no summary)'} (${s.link})`).join('\\n\\n');
      return [{ json: { digest, count: stories.length } }];"""
      
      PARSE_JS = """// Extract the LLM's JSON script (tolerates markdown fences / extra prose).
      const raw = ($json.choices && $json.choices[0] && $json.choices[0].message && $json.choices[0].message.content) || '';
      let text = String(raw).trim().replace(/^```(?:json)?/i, '').replace(/```$/, '').trim();
      let script = null;
      try { script = JSON.parse(text); } catch (e) {
        const m = text.match(/\\{[\\s\\S]*\\}/);
        if (m) script = JSON.parse(m[0]);
      }
      let segments = ((script && script.segments) || []).map((s) => String(s).trim()).filter(Boolean);
      if (!segments.length) {
        const digest = $('Build Digest').first().json.digest || '';
        segments = digest.split('\\n\\n').map((s) => s.replace(/\\(https?:\\/\\/\\S+\\)/, '').split(' - ')[0].trim()).filter(Boolean).slice(0, 8);
      }
      if (!segments.length) throw new Error('No script segments produced by the LLM.');
      const title = String((script && script.title) || 'Python News Roundup').slice(0, 80);
      return [{ json: { title, segments } }];"""
      
      SMOKE_SEGMENTS = [
          "This is a smoke test of your Python news pipeline.",
          "If you can read this, subtitles, rendering and the webhook all work.",
          "Now go wire up the local LLM and TTS for the real daily video.",
      ]
      
      
      def http(name, nid, pos, url, body, timeout=1800000):
          return {
              "parameters": {
                  "method": "POST", "url": url,
                  "sendBody": True, "specifyBody": "json",
                  "jsonBody": body,
                  "options": {"timeout": timeout},
              },
              "id": nid, "name": name,
              "type": "n8n-nodes-base.httpRequest", "typeVersion": 4.2,
              "position": pos,
          }
      
      
      def code(name, nid, pos, js):
          return {
              "parameters": {"mode": "runOnceForAllItems", "jsCode": js},
              "id": nid, "name": name,
              "type": "n8n-nodes-base.code", "typeVersion": 2,
              "position": pos,
          }
      
      
      def sticky(name, nid, pos, content, h, w, color):
          return {
              "parameters": {"content": content, "height": h, "width": w, "color": color},
              "id": nid, "name": name,
              "type": "n8n-nodes-base.stickyNote", "typeVersion": 1,
              "position": pos,
          }
      
      
      nodes = [
          sticky("Sticky - Setup", "a1", [-620, -200],
                 "## SETUP (one-time)\nOn the host, the render service must be running:\n```bash\npython3 ~/git-projects/ai-rss/render_server.py\n```\nIt serves POST /render (voicebox TTS -> ComfyUI background -> ffmpeg -> Telegram).\n\nSmoke test (no LLM/TTS/ComfyUI needed):\n```bash\ncurl -X POST http://localhost:5678/webhook/ai-rss/smoke -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{}'\n```", 480, 380, 4),
          sticky("Sticky - Your Prompt", "a2", [1180, -200],
                 "## EDIT ME\nReplace the marker in **Write Script (Local LLM)**:\n" + PROMPT_MARKER + "\nwith your own style notes.", 220, 320, 5),
      
          {
              "parameters": {"rule": {"interval": [{"field": "cron", "expression": "0 9 * * *"}]}},
              "id": "b1", "name": "Schedule (Daily 9AM)",
              "type": "n8n-nodes-base.scheduleTrigger", "typeVersion": 1.2,
              "position": [0, 0],
          },
          http("Fetch Python Stories (HN)", "b2", [220, 0],
               "https://hnrss.org/newest?q=python&count=30", "PLACEHOLDER_FETCH", 60000),
          {"parameters": {}, "id": "b3", "name": "Parse RSS",
           "type": "n8n-nodes-base.xml", "typeVersion": 1, "position": [440, 0]},
          code("Build Digest", "b4", [660, 0], DIGEST_JS),
          {
              "parameters": {
                  "method": "POST",
                  "url": "={{ ($env.LLM_BASE_URL || 'http://host.docker.internal:1234') + '/v1/chat/completions' }}",
                  "sendBody": True, "specifyBody": "json",
                  "jsonBody": "={{ JSON.stringify({ model: $env.LLM_MODEL || 'local-model', temperature: 0.8, messages: [ { role: 'system', content: " + json.dumps(SYSTEM_PROMPT) + " }, { role: 'user', content: 'Here are today\\'s Python stories:\\n\\n' + $json.digest + '\\n\\nWrite the video script now.' } ] }) }}",
                  "options": {"timeout": 120000},
              },
              "id": "b5", "name": "Write Script (Local LLM)",
              "type": "n8n-nodes-base.httpRequest", "typeVersion": 4.2,
              "position": [880, 0],
          },
          code("Parse Script & Cues", "b6", [1100, 0], PARSE_JS),
          http("Call Render Server", "b7", [1320, 0],
               "={{ ($env.RENDER_SERVER_URL || 'http://host.docker.internal:8777') + '/render' }}",
               "={{ JSON.stringify({ title: $json.title, segments: $json.segments }) }}"),
      
          {
              "parameters": {"httpMethod": "POST", "path": "ai-rss/smoke",
                             "responseMode": "responseNode", "options": {}},
              "id": "c1", "name": "Smoke Webhook",
              "type": "n8n-nodes-base.webhook", "typeVersion": 2,
              "position": [0, 300], "webhookId": "c7a10000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001",
          },
          http("Render Smoke", "c3", [220, 300],
               "={{ ($env.RENDER_SERVER_URL || 'http://host.docker.internal:8777') + '/render' }}",
               "={{ JSON.stringify({ title: 'Smoke Test - Python News', segments: " + json.dumps(SMOKE_SEGMENTS) + ", smoke: true }) }}"),
          {
              "parameters": {
                  "respondWith": "json",
                  "responseBody": "={{ JSON.stringify({ status: 'ok', smoke: true, video_path: $json.video_path, voice: $json.voice, background: $json.background, telegram: $json.telegram }) }}",
                  "options": {},
              },
              "id": "c4", "name": "Respond OK",
              "type": "n8n-nodes-base.respondToWebhook", "typeVersion": 1,
              "position": [440, 300],
          },
      ]
      
      # The HN fetch node needs file response so the XML node can parse raw bytes.
      for n in nodes:
          if n.get("name") == "Fetch Python Stories (HN)":
              n["parameters"] = {
                  "url": "https://hnrss.org/newest?q=python&count=30",
                  "options": {"response": {"response": {"responseFormat": "file"}}},
              }
              n["parameters"].pop("method", None)
              n["parameters"].pop("sendBody", None)
              n["parameters"].pop("specifyBody", None)
              n["parameters"].pop("jsonBody", None)
      
      chain = [
          ("Schedule (Daily 9AM)", "Fetch Python Stories (HN)"),
          ("Fetch Python Stories (HN)", "Parse RSS"),
          ("Parse RSS", "Build Digest"),
          ("Build Digest", "Write Script (Local LLM)"),
          ("Write Script (Local LLM)", "Parse Script & Cues"),
          ("Parse Script & Cues", "Call Render Server"),
          ("Smoke Webhook", "Render Smoke"),
          ("Render Smoke", "Respond OK"),
      ]
      
      connections = {}
      for src, dst in chain:
          connections.setdefault(src, {"main": [[{"node": dst, "type": "main", "index": 0}]]})
      
      workflow = {
          "name": "AI-RSS - Python News Video Generator",
          "nodes": nodes,
          "connections": connections,
          "settings": {"executionOrder": "v1"},
          "staticData": None,
          "meta": None,
          "tags": [],
      }
      
      out = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "workflow.json"
      out.write_text(json.dumps(workflow, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8")
      print(f"wrote {out} with {len(nodes)} nodes, {len(chain)} connections")
````

```
- path: notify_telegram.py
  content: |
      #!/usr/bin/env python3
      """Send a Telegram notification, optionally with the rendered video attached.
      
      Usage:
        notify_telegram.py --text "message"
        notify_telegram.py --text "message" --video /path/to/file.mp4
      
      Env: TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN, TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID (required).
      Stdlib-only. Exits 0 on success (or when Telegram is not configured — non-fatal),
      1 on a hard failure.
      """
      import argparse
      import os
      import sys
      import urllib.error
      import urllib.parse
      import urllib.request
      
      TOKEN = os.environ.get("TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN", "")
      CHAT_ID = os.environ.get("TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID", "")
      API = f"https://api.telegram.org/bot{TOKEN}"
      
      
      def not_configured() -> bool:
          if not TOKEN or not CHAT_ID or TOKEN.startswith("placeholder"):
              print("Telegram not configured (TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN/TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID) — skipping notification.")
              return True
          return False
      
      
      def post(url: str, data: bytes, content_type: str, timeout: int = 60) -> dict:
          req = urllib.request.Request(url, data=data, headers={"Content-Type": content_type})
          with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=timeout) as resp:
              return json.loads(resp.read())
      
      
      import json  # noqa: E402
      
      
      def send_message(text: str) -> None:
          body = urllib.parse.urlencode({"chat_id": CHAT_ID, "text": text}).encode()
          post(f"{API}/sendMessage", body, "application/x-www-form-urlencoded")
      
      
      def send_video(video_path: str, caption: str) -> None:
          boundary = "ai_rss_boundary_7f3d9b2c"
          with open(video_path, "rb") as f:
              video_bytes = f.read()
      
          def field(name: str, value: str) -> bytes:
              return (
                  f"--{boundary}\r\n"
                  f'Content-Disposition: form-data; name="{name}"\r\n\r\n'
                  f"{value}\r\n"
              ).encode()
      
          head = field("chat_id", CHAT_ID) + field("caption", caption)
          file_part = (
              f"--{boundary}\r\n"
              f'Content-Disposition: form-data; name="video"; filename="{os.path.basename(video_path)}"\r\n'
              f"Content-Type: video/mp4\r\n\r\n"
          ).encode()
          tail = f"\r\n--{boundary}--\r\n".encode()
      
          body = head + file_part + video_bytes + tail
          post(
              f"{API}/sendVideo",
              body,
              f"multipart/form-data; boundary={boundary}",
              timeout=300,
          )
      
      
      def main() -> None:
          ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Telegram notification for ai-rss renders")
          ap.add_argument("--text", required=True, help="message text (used as caption when --video is set)")
          ap.add_argument("--video", help="path to an mp4 to attach")
          args = ap.parse_args()
      
          if not_configured():
              sys.exit(0)
      
          try:
              if args.video and os.path.isfile(args.video):
                  size = os.path.getsize(args.video)
                  if size <= 50 * 1024 * 1024:
                      send_video(args.video, args.text)
                      print(f"Telegram: video sent ({size / 1e6:.1f} MB)")
                  else:
                      send_message(args.text + f"\n\n(video too large for Telegram: {size / 1e6:.1f} MB — {args.video})")
                      print("Telegram: text sent (video over 50 MB limit)")
              else:
                  send_message(args.text)
                  print("Telegram: message sent")
          except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
              print(f"ERROR: Telegram API {e.code}: {e.read().decode(errors='replace')[:300]}", file=sys.stderr)
              sys.exit(1)
          except Exception as e:
              print(f"ERROR: Telegram send failed: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
              sys.exit(1)
      
      
      if __name__ == "__main__":
          main()
```

> _Reasoning_
> The execution data is stored in n8n's flattened JSON format. Let me write a small resolver that reconstructs the JSON structure. The format is a classic "json-patch-like" flat array format: index 0 is a template {"version":1,"startData":"1",...} where values that are strings of digits are references to array positions. So "startData": "1" refers to element 1, etc. I need to recursively resolve: if a value is a string matching ^\d+$ and int < len(arr), replace with arr[int]. But careful: legitimate string values that are digits would be wrongly resolved... in this flattened format, all digit strings are refs. n8n uses this for compressing JSON in the DB (it's the "jsonStringify" format from `@n8n/json`? Actually it's the flat format from `json-stringify` library used by n8n for execution data: arrays where strings that look like numbers are pointers).
> 
> Let me write a resolver: 
> 
> def resolve(x):
>   if isinstance(x, str) and x.isdigit() and int(x) < len(arr):
>      # it's a pointer
>      return resolve(arr[int(x)])
>   if isinstance(x, list): return [resolve(i) for i in x]
>   if isinstance(x, dict): return {k: resolve(v) for k,v in x.items()}
>   return x
> 
> Start with arr[0] and resolve. The pointers are index into the top-level array. This should reconstruct the full structure. Then dig into resultData.error and runData.
> 
> Then extract the error message. Also check lastNodeExecuted.

The execution data is in n8n's flattened pointer format. Let me resolve it properly:

**🛠 Run Terminal Command**

```json
{
  "command": "docker exec -i n8n-n8n-1 python3 - <<'EOF'\nimport sqlite3, json\ndb = sqlite3.connect(\"file:/home/node/.n8n/database.sqlite?mode=ro\", uri=True)\ncur = db.cursor()\n\ndef unflatten(arr):\n    def r(x):\n        if isinstance(x, str) and x.isdigit() and int(x) < len(arr):\n            return r(arr[int(x)])\n        if isinstance(x, list): return [r(i) for i in x]\n        if isinstance(x, dict): return {k: r(v) for k, v in x.items()}\n        return x\n    return r(arr[0])\n\nfor eid in (215, 214):\n    row = cur.execute(\"SELECT data FROM execution_data WHERE executionId=?\", (eid,)).fetchone()\n    arr = json.loads(row[0])\n    d = unflatten(arr)\n    rd = d.get(\"resultData\", {})\n    print(f\"===== execution {eid} | lastNodeExecuted: {rd.get('lastNodeExecuted')} =====\")\n    err = rd.get(\"error\") or {}\n    print(\"top error:\", json.dumps(err, indent=1)[:600])\n    for node, runs in (rd.get(\"runData\") or {}).items():\n        for run in runs:\n            e = run.get(\"error\")\n            if e:\n                print(f\"--- node [{node}] error ---\")\n                print(json.dumps(e, indent=1)[:800])\nEOF",
  "process_type": "SYNC",
  "timeout_seconds": 30
}
```

> _Reasoning_
> My unflatten function recursed infinitely because a digit string can point to itself or a cycle (e.g. index "8" points to "8" or a string "5" that resolves to something containing "5"). Need cycle protection: track visited indices on the current path.
> 
> Let me write a safer version with memoization by index — resolve each index once, memoize the result. Use a dict of resolved values; resolve indices in order, and when encountering a digit string, replace with resolved value of that index if already computed... but the ordering might have forward references. Simplest: iterative resolution with memo + visited set to break cycles:
> 
> def resolve(idx, seen): if idx in seen: return None; ...
> 
> Actually easier: n8n's "flatten" format: each string of digits is a pointer into the top array. Resolve with memoization and cycle detection:
> 
> def load(i): 
>   if i in memo: return memo[i]
>   v = arr[i]
>   if isinstance(v, str) and v.isdigit() and int(v) != i: 
>       memo[i] = load(int(v))
>   else: memo[i] = v
>   return memo[i]
> 
> Wait but a pointer could be forward ("5" at index 2 pointing to index 5). Recursion handles forward refs; cycles broken by memo check before recursing — but cycle where i->j and j->i: memo doesn't break it. Use "in progress" set.
> 
> Also there's a subtlety: digit strings inside resolved values should NOT be treated as pointers — only pointers at positions where n8n put them. When you load arr[i], if arr[i] is a digit string, it's a pointer to arr[int]... but a legit string value "123" would be ambiguous. n8n's jsonStringifySimple stores actual strings differently? In their format, real strings that look like numbers... they encode them... I don't remember exactly. Practically: strings like "b80d8608..." are hashes, messages are longer. > **Root cause of "start.sh doesn't start scraping/generating videos":**
> 
> 1. The smoke webhook path (`./start.sh smoke`) fails at the **"Render Smoke"** HTTP node with **"access to env vars denied"** because the node URL uses `$env.RENDER_SERVER_URL` and n8n restricts `$env` access in expressions unless `N8N_BLOCK_ENV_ACCESS_IN_NODE=false` (or allowlist env feature is enabled). Default n8n behavior: env access in expressions is blocked unless configured.
> 
> 2. The **daily 9AM schedule never fired** — no executions from mode 'trigger'/'schedule' at all. The workflow is active=1 in the DB... but why no schedule executions? Possibly because the activation failed or the workflow was updated while active and the scheduler didn't re-register the trigger... OR because the container restarted 36 min ago and the schedule only fires at 9AM (it's now ~10:30 AM; container restarted at 09:52ish; the schedule for today at 09:00 — container was up then? "Up 36 minutes" at ~10:28 → container started ~09:52, so 09:00 firing was before the restart but after boot at 09:48. Hmm, the host booted at 09:48 today, so 09:00 didn't happen while booted. Yesterday the workflow updatedAt was 2026-09-29 10:16 — activated at 10:16, so 9AM yesterday already passed. So the schedule simply hasn't had a 9AM since activation — today it would fire at 9AM but the host was rebooting at 09:48 (boot after 9AM). So the schedule *may actually work tomorrow*. But we can't be sure — the user says it doesn't start scraping/generating.
> 
> Actually wait — also important: the "Fetch Python Stories (HN)" node etc. all sit behind the Schedule trigger. The only test path is the smoke webhook, which fails on `$env`. So from the user's perspective: "start.sh doesn't start scrapping and generating videos" — they run ./start.sh, everything says up, but nothing ever generates.
> 
> Two fixes needed:
> 1. Remove `$env.*` usage from node expressions (replace with literal fallback `http://host.docker.internal:8777` or use n8n config env vars via docker-compose environment, which are different from $env in expressions). Simplest robust fix: hardcode URLs in the workflow (they're stable: host.docker.internal:8777 and :1234), and let the env override happen at build time in build_workflow.py (i.e., read os.environ in the Python builder, not at n8n runtime).
> 2. Optionally set `N8N_BLOCK_ENV_ACCESS_IN_NODE=false` in docker-compose, but editing compose requires restart; hardcoding is cleaner and works immediately.
> 
> Also verify: does the smoke failure also mean the daily chain would fail? The daily chain's "Call Render Server" and "Write Script (Local LLM)" nodes also use $env — same failure. So yes, the whole pipeline is broken by $env denial. That's THE bug.

## 🔍 Analysis

**1. Why scraping/video generation doesn't run from n8n:**
- All services are healthy, the workflow **is active**, and container→host networking works (render :8777 and llama :1234 both reachable).
- **Root cause:** the n8n workflow's HTTP nodes build URLs with expressions like `$env.RENDER_SERVER_URL || 'http://host.docker.internal:8777'`. n8n **denies `$env` access in expressions by default** → every run dies in ~80ms with `access to env vars denied` (executions #214, #215 both failed at the "Render Smoke" node).

```
      import io
      import json as _json
      import logging

      from datetime import datetime
      from pathlib import Path
      
      from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, File, Form, HTTPException, UploadFile
      from fastapi.responses import FileResponse, StreamingResponse
      from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
      
      from .. import config, models
      from ..app import safe_content_disposition
      from ..database import VoiceProfile as DBVoiceProfile, get_db
      from ..services import channels, export_import, personality, profiles
      from ..services.profiles import _profile_to_response
      
      logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
      
      router = APIRouter()
      
      
      @router.post("/profiles", response_model=models.VoiceProfileResponse)
      async def create_profile(
          data: models.VoiceProfileCreate,
          db: Session = Depends(get_db),
      ):
          """Create a new voice profile."""
          try:
              return await profiles.create_profile(data, db)
          except ValueError as e:
              raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail=str(e))
          except Exception as e:
              raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail=str(e))
      
      
      @router.get("/profiles", response_model=list[models.VoiceProfileResponse])
      async def list_profiles(db: Session = Depends(get_db)):
          """List all voice profiles."""
          return await profiles.list_profiles(db)
      
      
      @router.post("/profiles/import", response_model=models.VoiceProfileResponse)
      async def import_profile(
          file: UploadFile = File(...),
          db: Session = Depends(get_db),
      ):
          """Import a voice profile from a ZIP archive."""
          MAX_FILE_SIZE = 100 * 1024 * 1024
      
          content = await file.read()
      
          if len(content) > MAX_FILE_SIZE:
              raise HTTPException(
                  status_code=400, detail=f"File too large. Maximum size is {MAX_FILE_SIZE / (1024 * 1024)}MB"
              )
      
          try:
              profile = await export_import.import_profile_from_zip(content, db)
              return profile
          except ValueError as e:
              raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail=str(e))
          except Exception as e:
              raise HTTPException(status_code=500, detail=str(e))
      
      
      # ── Preset Voice Endpoints ───────────────────────────────────────────
      # These MUST be declared before /profiles/{profile_id} to avoid the
      # wildcard swallowing "presets" as a profile_id.
      
      
      @router.get("/profiles/presets/{engine}")

          """List available preset voices for an engine."""
          if engine == "kokoro":
```

```
      def _get_preset_voice_ids(engine: str) -> set[str]:
          if engine == "kokoro":
              from ..backends.kokoro_backend import KOKORO_VOICES
      
              return {voice_id for voice_id, _name, _gender, _lang in KOKORO_VOICES}
      
          if engine == "qwen_custom_voice":
              from ..backends.qwen_custom_voice_backend import QWEN_CUSTOM_VOICES
      
              return {voice_id for voice_id, _name, _gender, _lang, _desc in QWEN_CUSTOM_VOICES}
      
          return set()
      
      
      def _validate_profile_fields(
          *,
          voice_type: str,
          preset_engine: str | None,
          preset_voice_id: str | None,
          design_prompt: str | None,
          default_engine: str | None,
      ) -> str | None:
          if voice_type == "preset":
              if not preset_engine or not preset_voice_id:
                  return "Preset profiles require both preset_engine and preset_voice_id"
              if default_engine and default_engine != preset_engine:
                  return "Preset profiles must use their preset_engine as default_engine"
      
              available_voice_ids = _get_preset_voice_ids(preset_engine)
              if available_voice_ids and preset_voice_id not in available_voice_ids:
                  return f"Preset voice '{preset_voice_id}' is not valid for engine '{preset_engine}'"
              return None
      
          if voice_type == "designed":
              if not design_prompt or not design_prompt.strip():
                  return "Designed profiles require a design_prompt"
              if preset_engine or preset_voice_id:
                  return "Designed profiles cannot set preset_engine or preset_voice_id"
              return None
      
          if preset_engine or preset_voice_id:
              return "Cloned profiles cannot set preset_engine or preset_voice_id"
          if design_prompt:
              return "Cloned profiles cannot set design_prompt"
          if default_engine and default_engine not in CLONING_ENGINES:
              return f"Cloned profiles cannot use default engine '{default_engine}'"
          return None
      
      
      def validate_profile_engine(profile, engine: str) -> None:
          voice_type = getattr(profile, "voice_type", None) or "cloned"
      
          if voice_type == "preset":
              preset_engine = getattr(profile, "preset_engine", None)
              preset_voice_id = getattr(profile, "preset_voice_id", None)
              if not preset_engine or not preset_voice_id:
                  raise ValueError(f"Preset profile {profile.id} is missing preset engine metadata")
              if preset_engine != engine:
                  raise ValueError(
                      f"Preset profile {profile.id} only supports engine '{preset_engine}', not '{engine}'"
                  )
```

```
      async def update_profile(
          profile_id: str,
          data: VoiceProfileCreate,
          db: Session,
      ) -> VoiceProfileResponse | None:
          """
          Update a voice profile.
      
          Args:
              profile_id: Profile ID
              data: Updated profile data
              db: Database session
      
          Returns:
              Updated profile or None if not found
      
          Raises:
              ValueError: If a profile with the same name already exists (different profile)
          """
          profile = db.query(DBVoiceProfile).filter_by(id=profile_id).first()
          if not profile:
              return None
      
          if profile.name != data.name:
              existing_profile = db.query(DBVoiceProfile).filter_by(name=data.name).first()
              if existing_profile:
                  raise ValueError(f"A profile with the name '{data.name}' already exists. Please choose a different name.")
      
          voice_type = getattr(profile, "voice_type", None) or "cloned"
          preset_engine = getattr(profile, "preset_engine", None)
          preset_voice_id = getattr(profile, "preset_voice_id", None)
          design_prompt = getattr(profile, "design_prompt", None)
          default_engine = data.default_engine if data.default_engine is not None else getattr(profile, "default_engine", None)
      
          validation_error = _validate_profile_fields(
              voice_type=voice_type,
              preset_engine=preset_engine,
              preset_voice_id=preset_voice_id,
              design_prompt=design_prompt,
              default_engine=default_engine,
          )
          if validation_error:
              raise ValueError(validation_error)
      
          profile.name = data.name
          profile.description = data.description
          profile.language = data.language
          profile.personality = data.personality
          if data.default_engine is not None:
              profile.default_engine = data.default_engine or None  # empty string → NULL
          profile.updated_at = datetime.utcnow()
      
          db.commit()
          db.refresh(profile)
      
          return _profile_to_response(profile)
      
      
      async def delete_profile(
          profile_id: str,

      ) -> bool:
          """
          Delete a voice profile and all associated data.
      
          Args:
              profile_id: Profile ID
              db: Database session
      
          Returns:
              True if deleted, False if not found
          """
          profile = db.query(DBVoiceProfile).filter_by(id=profile_id).first()
          if not profile:
```

````
- path: start.sh
  content: |
      #!/usr/bin/env bash
      # ai-rss — start the full local stack (all offline-capable once models are cached)
      #
      #   ./start.sh           start everything
      #   ./start.sh status    show what's running
      #   ./start.sh stop      stop everything
      #   ./start.sh video     render a test video right now
      #   ./start.sh smoke     full end-to-end test through n8n's webhook
      #
      # Services:
      #   llama-server    :1234   LLM that writes the script (Llama 3.2 3B, local GGUF)
      #   comfyui         :8188   SD-Turbo AI backgrounds (CPU)
      #   voicebox        :17493  kokoro TTS voiceover (CPU)
      #   ai-rss-render   :8777   render bridge n8n talks to
      #   n8n             :5678   workflow orchestrator (docker compose)
      
      set -u
      
      UNITS=(llama-server comfyui voicebox ai-rss-render)
      N8N_DIR="$HOME/docker/n8n"
      
      is_up() { curl -s --max-time 3 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' "$1" 2>/dev/null | grep -q 200; }
      
      wait_for() { # wait_for <name> <url> <tries>
        local name="$1" url="$2" tries="${3:-30}"
        for _ in $(seq 1 "$tries"); do
          is_up "$url" && { echo "  ✓ $name is up ($url)"; return 0; }
          sleep 2
        done
        echo "  ✗ $name did not come up at $url" >&2
        return 1
      }
      
      start() {
        echo "Starting ai-rss stack..."
        for u in "${UNITS[@]}"; do
          systemctl --user enable --now "$u.service" >/dev/null 2>&1
          systemctl --user start "$u.service" 2>/dev/null
        done
        if docker compose -f "$N8N_DIR/docker-compose.yml" ps -q n8n 2>/dev/null | grep -q .; then
          echo "  ✓ n8n container already running"
        else
          (cd "$N8N_DIR" && docker compose up -d) >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo "  ✓ n8n container started"
        fi
        wait_for "llama-server"  "http://127.0.0.1:1234/health"
        wait_for "comfyui"       "http://127.0.0.1:8188/system_stats"
        wait_for "voicebox"      "http://127.0.0.1:17493/health"
        wait_for "render server" "http://127.0.0.1:8777/health"
        wait_for "n8n"           "http://localhost:5678/healthz"
        echo ""
        echo "Stack ready."
        echo "  - Render a video now:   ./start.sh video"
        echo "  - Full webhook test:    ./start.sh smoke"
        echo "  - Daily schedule:       n8n fires automatically at 9:00 AM"
      }
      
      stop() {
        echo "Stopping ai-rss stack..."
        for u in "${UNITS[@]}"; do systemctl --user stop "$u.service" 2>/dev/null; done
        (cd "$N8N_DIR" && docker compose stop) >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo "  ✓ all stopped"
      }
      
      status() {
        printf "%-14s %-8s %s\n" "SERVICE" "STATE" "ENDPOINT"
        for u in "${UNITS[@]}"; do
          printf "%-14s %-8s %s\n" "$u" "$(systemctl --user is-active "$u.service" 2>/dev/null || echo '?')"
        done
        printf "%-14s %-8s %s\n" "n8n" "$(docker compose -f "$N8N_DIR/docker-compose.yml" ps n8n 2>/dev/null | grep -q n8n && echo active || echo inactive)" "http://localhost:5678"
        echo ""
        is_up "http://127.0.0.1:1234/health"          && echo "  ✓ LLM responding"
        is_up "http://127.0.0.1:8188/system_stats"    && echo "  ✓ ComfyUI responding"
        is_up "http://127.0.0.1:17493/health"         && echo "  ✓ voicebox responding"
        is_up "http://127.0.0.1:8777/health"          && echo "  ✓ render server responding"
      }
      
      video() {
        echo "Rendering a video via the render server (LLM-free manual script)..."
        curl -s --max-time 560 -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8777/render \
          -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
          -d '{
            "title": "Manual Test Video",
            "segments": [
              "Spuds, this is a manual render straight from start.sh.",
              "Voiceover comes from kokoro, background from SD-Turbo, all on your CPU.",
              "Drop a comment if this is crisp enough. This is Potaterrr - stay crispy."
            ]
          }'
        echo
      }
      
      smoke() {
        echo "Firing n8n smoke webhook (full daily path minus the LLM)..."
        curl -s --max-time 560 -X POST http://localhost:5678/webhook/ai-rss/smoke \
          -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{}'
        echo
      }
      
      case "${1:-start}" in
        start)  start ;;
        stop)   stop ;;
        status) status ;;
        video)  video ;;
        smoke)  smoke ;;
        *) echo "usage: $0 {start|stop|status|video|smoke}"; exit 1 ;;
      esac
      
  referencedBy: {}
- path: readme.md
  content: |
      
      Everything render-side is **stdlib-only Python** — no pip deps on the host.
      Failures degrade gracefully: no voicebox → silent video, no ComfyUI → gradient background, no Telegram → skipped.
      
      ## 📥 Setup
      
      ### 1. Services (all systemd user units, auto-start on boot)
      - **n8n**: `~/docker/n8n` compose, custom image `n8n-with-renderer` (n8n + static python3 + ffmpeg, repo mounted at `/data/ai-rss`, output at `/data/generated`).
      - **Render server**: `ai-rss-render.service` — HTTP bridge on :8777 (n8n calls this).
      - **ComfyUI**: `comfyui.service` — `--cpu`, :8188, model `sd_turbo.safetensors`.
      - **voicebox**: `voicebox.service` — :17493, engine kokoro (CPU-friendly), profile `potaterrr` (voice `af_bella`).
      - **llama-server**: `llama-server.service` — llama.cpp on :1234, `Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct-Q4_K_M` (local GGUF in `~/git-clones/llama.cpp/models/`).
      
      Everything is **fully offline** once models are cached (they are). Control it all with:
      ```bash
      ./start.sh          # start the whole stack + wait until healthy
      ./start.sh status   # what's running
      ./start.sh video    # render a video right now (manual script)
      ./start.sh smoke    # fire the n8n smoke webhook
      ./start.sh stop     # stop everything
      ```
      
      All three units live in this repo and are installed to `~/.config/systemd/user/` (linger enabled).
      
      ```bash
      systemctl --user status ai-rss-render comfyui voicebox
      curl localhost:8188/system_stats           # ComfyUI
      curl localhost:17493/health                # voicebox
      ```
      
      voicebox first-time setup (one-off, already done): Python **3.12** venv via uv (kokoro needs <3.13), CPU torch, `backend/requirements.txt`, then `chatterbox-tts`/`hume-tada` with `--no-deps`. The `potaterrr` voice profile (kokoro/af_bella) already exists.
      
      llama.cpp first-time setup (one-off, already done): model GGUF lives in `~/git-clones/llama.cpp/models/`; unit runs `llama-server --port 1234 --ctx-size 8192 --threads 6`.
      
      ### 2. n8n workflow

      ### 3. Telegram
````

> 
> Why: the Fetch node is configured with `responseFormat: file` — in that mode, the HTTP Request node outputs the file as **binary** data (property `data` in binary), not JSON. The XML node then needs to read from binary. The XML node's default "dataPropertyName" is `data` — it looks for `json.data`? Actually for n8n XML node, it reads from a property of the item. With responseFormat file, output item has `binary.data` (base64 or binary buffer) and `json` is empty `{}`. The XML node (typeVersion 1) parameters: `dataPropertyName` (default "data") — it reads `item.json[data]`?? Hmm. In older n8n XML node, source is `json` property named `data`. The error "Item has no JSON property called data" confirms it looks in **json** for property `data`, but the fetch node put the file in **binary**.
> 
> This workflow previously had this exact config and... did the schedule path ever work? Executions show only webhook smoke runs (214, 215, 216) and nothing scheduled — so the full chain has likely never run successfully. The smoke path bypassed Fetch/Parse. So this Parse RSS issue is a latent bug too.
> 
> Fix options:
> 1. Change Fetch node response format to `json` — then n8n auto-parses? No — HN RSS returns XML; with responseFormat json it would fail to parse as JSON. Keep `file`.
> 2. Configure Parse RSS to read from binary: n8n's XML node (typeVersion 1) parameters include `dataPropertyName` and also `options`... The XML node reads from `binary` if the property is binary? In n8n, the XML node docs: "Data Property Name: field containing the XML to parse (in json or binary)". Modern versions check binary first. The error says "no JSON property called data" — meaning this version's XML node only looks at json. So set Fetch node's response to keep body as text in json: responseFormat "text"! Then item.json.data = XML string, and XML node parses json.data. 
> 
> Option: responseFormat: "text" → JSON property `data` contains the raw XML text → XML node with dataPropertyName "data" reads json.data. That should work.
> 
> Let me update build_workflow.py: in the fetch-node fixup loop, change responseFormat from "file" to "text".

> Wait — does the XML node accept a plain XML string from json property? Yes: "The XML node converts XML data to JSON and vice versa. Field containing the XML". With text response, json.data is the XML string.

> Also the DIGEST_JS reads $json.rss.channel... — the XML node output shape: it converts XML → JSON object. The output may be under `json.rss` directly (if root is rss). DIGEST_JS handles `$json.rss.channel` — presumably that was designed for this XML node output. Keep as is.

All done! Here's the full summary:

## 🔍 What was broken (analysis)

`start.sh` itself was fine — all services started. The pipeline never ran because of **n8n configuration bugs** that only triggered when the workflow actually executed:

1. **`access to env vars denied`** — the HTTP nodes used `$env.RENDER_SERVER_URL` / `$env.LLM_BASE_URL` / `$env.LLM_MODEL` in expressions. n8n denies `$env` in expressions by default, so every webhook run died in ~80ms.
2. **Wrong RSS fetch format** — the HN fetch node returned `file` (binary) but the XML node reads `json.data` → `Parse RSS` crashed on the first full run.
3. **LLM timeout too short** — llama.cpp on your CPU generates at ~2.9 tok/s, so the script takes 3–5 min, but the node timed out at 120s and aborted generation mid-stream.
4. No way to trigger a full run from `start.sh` (only manual `video` and LLM-free `smoke`).

## 🔧 Fixes applied (all in `build_workflow.py`, pushed to the live workflow via n8n API)

- Hardcoded `http://host.docker.internal:8777/render` and `:1234/v1/chat/completions` (env fallbacks never worked anyway)
- RSS fetch → `responseFormat: text` so the XML node can parse it
- LLM node timeout 120s → **10 min**
- Added an IF node so `POST /webhook/ai-rss/smoke` with `{"full": true}` runs the **complete** pipeline — and new `./start.sh run` command

## 🎙️ Voice changed

Profile `potaterrr` recreated with kokoro **am_fenrir** (bright, playful male). Voicebox's update API doesn't apply preset changes, so it was delete + recreate — same name, zero code changes needed.

## ✍️ Prompt rewritten

Punchier hype style: scroll-stopping hook (≤10 words), segments ≤25 words, "strong verbs, short sentences," one hot take max, `spuds` kept, sign-off kept exactly: *"This is Potaterrr - stay crispy, spuds."* To tweak it later, edit `SYSTEM_PROMPT` in `build_workflow.py` and follow the readme's push command.

## ✅ Verified end-to-end

Exec #219: scraped HN → LLM wrote *"Rev up your Python game with 3 awesome new tools"* → Fenrir voiceover → ComfyUI background → `ai_rss_20260930_111353.mp4` (13 min) → **Telegram: sent**. Check your Telegram for the video!

# Agent Reach — internet capability router

15 platforms, multiple backends each. **When this skill exists, use it for
these platforms — do not invent your own approach.**

## Standing rules (apply for the whole session)

1. **Health-check before acting**: for multi-backend/login-backed platforms (XiaoHongShu /
   Reddit / Bilibili / Twitter / Facebook / Instagram), run `agent-reach doctor --json` first.
   Use a populated `active_backend`; `active_backend: null` means Doctor deliberately skipped a
   live probe to avoid browser-cookie reads or remote writes, not that no backend exists. Only when
   the user's task requires that platform, run the reference's read-only command to verify it.
2. **Announce what you use**: say "using agent-reach, platform X via backend Y"
   before starting.
3. **On failure, follow the retry chains in references/** — never guess
   commands.
4. **For broad research tasks**: combine platforms (Exa for web search +
   Twitter/Reddit for discussions + XiaoHongShu/Bilibili for Chinese
   perspectives), collect in parallel, then synthesize.
5. **Watch versions for the user**: after finishing a substantial

   If a new version exists, append one line to your wrap-up: "Agent Reach

## Login-backed platforms (pick by doctor's active_backend)

Twitter boundary: cookies saved by `agent-reach configure twitter-cookies`
are used only by `doctor` to check whether explicit credentials are present.
`doctor` does not run `twitter status` or configure the current shell. Before
calling `twitter` directly, explicitly provide `TWITTER_AUTH_TOKEN` and
`TWITTER_CT0` in the child-process environment without logging their values.

XiaoHongShu boundary: Agent Reach must not log the user in or read browser
cookies. OpenCLI may use only an existing Chrome session explicitly controlled
by the user. If none exists, do not automate login; use a manual Cookie-Editor
export with xiaohongshu-mcp or a legacy tool instead.

```bash
# Twitter search (twitter-cli preferred; retry chain in social.md)
twitter search "query" -n 10

# Reddit (NO zero-config path — OpenCLI or rdt-cli, login required)
opencli reddit search "query" -f yaml   # desktop
rdt search "query" --limit 10            # legacy/server

# XiaoHongShu (desktop prefers OpenCLI)

# Facebook / Instagram (desktop OpenCLI, browser session)

opencli facebook groups -f yaml
opencli instagram search "query" -f yaml       # user search
opencli instagram user USERNAME -f yaml        # recent posts from one user
```

When the routing table lacks a needed platform or command, run `opencli list`,
then inspect `opencli <platform> --help`. Discovery proves only that an adapter
exists, not that authentication or target content works. Run read-only commands
only when the user's task requires that platform, and require non-empty content.

**Never create files in the agent workspace.** Use `/tmp/` for temporary
output and `~/.agent-reach/` for persistent data.

```
- path: comfy_bg.py
  content: |
      #!/usr/bin/env python3
      """Generate a vertical AI background image via a local ComfyUI server and save it as PNG.
      
      Usage: comfy_bg.py <output.png> [prompt]
      
      Env: COMFY_BASE_URL (default http://127.0.0.1:8188)
           COMFY_CHECKPOINT (default sd_turbo.safetensors)
      Stdlib-only. Exits 0 on success, 1 on failure (caller falls back to the gradient).
      """
      import json
      import os
      import sys
      import time
      import urllib.parse
      import urllib.request
      
      BASE = os.environ.get("COMFY_BASE_URL", "http://127.0.0.1:8188").rstrip("/")
      CHECKPOINT = os.environ.get("COMFY_CHECKPOINT", "sd_turbo.safetensors")
      
      DEFAULT_PROMPT = (
          "dark futuristic technology newsroom background, glowing circuit patterns, "
          "deep navy and purple gradient lighting, cinematic bokeh, no text, vertical"
      )
      
      
      def main() -> None:
          if len(sys.argv) < 2:
              print("usage: comfy_bg.py <output.png> [prompt]", file=sys.stderr)
              sys.exit(1)
          out_path = sys.argv[1]
          prompt = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else DEFAULT_PROMPT
      
          # SD-Turbo: 1-step, free guidance scale 1.0 — tuned for fast CPU generation.
          workflow = {
              "1": {"class_type": "CheckpointLoaderSimple", "inputs": {"ckpt_name": CHECKPOINT}},
              "2": {"class_type": "CLIPTextEncode", "inputs": {"text": prompt, "clip": ["1", 1]}},
              "3": {"class_type": "CLIPTextEncode", "inputs": {"text": "", "clip": ["1", 1]}},
              "4": {"class_type": "EmptyLatentImage", "inputs": {"width": 1080, "height": 1920, "batch_size": 1}},
              "5": {"class_type": "KSampler", "inputs": {
                  "seed": int(time.time()),
                  "steps": 1,
                  "cfg": 1.0,
                  "sampler_name": "euler",
                  "scheduler": "simple",
                  "denoise": 1.0,
                  "model": ["1", 0],
                  "positive": ["2", 0],
                  "negative": ["3", 0],
                  "latent_image": ["4", 0],
              }},
              "6": {"class_type": "VAEDecode", "inputs": {"samples": ["5", 0], "vae": ["1", 2]}},
              "7": {"class_type": "SaveImage", "inputs": {"filename_prefix": "ai_rss_bg", "images": ["6", 0]}},
          }
      
          try:
              req = urllib.request.Request(
                  f"{BASE}/prompt",
                  data=json.dumps({"prompt": workflow}).encode("utf-8"),
                  headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"},
              )
              with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=30) as resp:
                  prompt_id = json.loads(resp.read())["prompt_id"]
          except Exception as e:
              print(f"ERROR: cannot reach ComfyUI at {BASE}: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
              sys.exit(1)
      
          # Poll history until the run finishes (SD-Turbo on CPU: ~30-90s).
          deadline = time.time() + 600
          while time.time() < deadline:
              try:
                  with urllib.request.urlopen(f"{BASE}/history/{prompt_id}", timeout=15) as resp:
                      history = json.loads(resp.read())
              except Exception:
                  time.sleep(2)
                  continue
              entry = history.get(prompt_id)
              if not entry:
                  time.sleep(2)
                  continue
              outputs = entry.get("outputs", {})
              for node_out in outputs.values():
                  for img in node_out.get("images", []):
                      url = f"{BASE}/view?filename={urllib.parse.quote(img['filename'])}&subfolder={urllib.parse.quote(img.get('subfolder',''))}&type={img.get('type','output')}"
                      try:
                          with urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=60) as r:
                              data = r.read()
                          with open(out_path, "wb") as f:
                              f.write(data)
                          print(f"BG_PATH={out_path}")
                          sys.exit(0)
                      except Exception as e:
                          print(f"ERROR: image download failed: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
                          sys.exit(1)
              # entry exists but no images yet
              time.sleep(2)
          print("ERROR: ComfyUI generation timed out", file=sys.stderr)
          sys.exit(1)
      
      
      if __name__ == "__main__":
          main()
      
  referencedBy: {}
```

# Agent Reach — internet capability router

15 platforms, multiple backends each. **When this skill exists, use it for
these platforms — do not invent your own approach.**

## Standing rules (apply for the whole session)

1. **Health-check before acting**: for multi-backend/login-backed platforms (XiaoHongShu /
   Reddit / Bilibili / Twitter / Facebook / Instagram), run `agent-reach doctor --json` first.
   Use a populated `active_backend`; `active_backend: null` means Doctor deliberately skipped a
   live probe to avoid browser-cookie reads or remote writes, not that no backend exists. Only when
   the user's task requires that platform, run the reference's read-only command to verify it.
2. **Announce what you use**: say "using agent-reach, platform X via backend Y"
   before starting.
3. **On failure, follow the retry chains in references/** — never guess
   commands.
4. **For broad research tasks**: combine platforms (Exa for web search +
   Twitter/Reddit for discussions + XiaoHongShu/Bilibili for Chinese
   perspectives), collect in parallel, then synthesize.
5. **Watch versions for the user**: after finishing a substantial
   multi-platform task, run `agent-reach check-update` (fast, one API call).
   If a new version exists, append one line to your wrap-up: "Agent Reach
   vX.Y.Z is available — paste this to me to update: 帮我更新 Agent Reach：
   https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Panniantong/agent-reach/main/docs/update.md".
   Never interrupt the current task to update; never nag about the same version twice.

time.sleep(3)\n    raise RuntimeError(\"ComfyUI generation timed out\")\n\n\ndef main() -> None:\n    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=\"ComfyUI img2img (character/style transfer)\")\n    ap.add_argument(\"out\", help=\"output PNG path\")\n    ap.add_argument(\"prompt\", nargs=\"?\", default=DEFAULT_PROMPT)\n    ap.add_argument(\"--image\", default=str(Path.home() / \"Downloads\" / \"pfp.jpeg\"))\n    ap.add_argument(\"--denoise\", type=float, default=0.55)\n    ap.add_argument(\"--steps\", type=int, default=4)\n    ap.add_argument(\"--width\", type=int, default=1080)\n    ap.add_argument(\"--height\", type=int, default=1920)\n    ap.add_argument(\"--fit\", choices=[\"pad\", \"cover\", \"stretch\"], default=\"pad\")\n    ap.add_argument(\"--timeout\", type=int, default=900, help=\"seconds to wait for ComfyUI\")\n    args = ap.parse_args()\n\n    if not os.path.isfile(args.image):\n        print(f\"ERROR: source image not found: {args.image}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        sys.exit(1)\n\n    try:\n        png = fit_image(args.image, args.width, args.height, args.fit)\n        name = upload(png)\n        prompt_id = run(args.prompt, name, args.steps, args.denoise)\n        fetch(prompt_id, args.out, args.timeout)\n    except Exception as e:\n        print(f\"ERROR: {e}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        sys.exit(1)\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    main()\n"

> What happened: my parse flow is:
> 1. `json.loads(text)` — failed silently (caught)

> The LLM output contains a raw newline INSIDE a JSON string (e.g. "sentence with\nnewline"). Standard JSON forbids raw control chars in strings. Python's `json.loads` has `strict=False` option which allows control characters inside strings! `json.loads(s, strict=False)` — that fixes exactly this.

> Also the n8n PARSE_JS has the same vulnerability in principle, but Code node can tolerate... let me fix generate_news.py:
> 
> ```python
> try:
>     script = json.loads(text, strict=False)
> except Exception:
>     m = re.search(r"\{[\s\S]*\}", text)
>     if m:
>         script = json.loads(m[0], strict=False)
> ```
> 
> `strict=False` allows literal control characters (newlines/tabs) inside strings — perfect for sloppy LLM JSON. That's the minimal robust fix.
> 
> The dry-run earlier succeeded, so this is intermittent LLM behavior — worth hardening. Fix now, then relaunch the unit.

Found it — the LLM emitted a **raw newline inside a JSON string**, which strict JSON rejects. Python has a built-in fix: `json.loads(..., strict=False)` tolerates control characters in strings. Hardening the parser:

**🛠 Str Replace**

```json
{
  "path": "generate_news.py",
  "replacements": [
    {
      "oldString": "    script = None\n    try:\n        script = json.loads(text)\n    except Exception:\n        m = re.search(r\"\\{[\\s\\S]*\\}\", text)\n        if m:\n            script = json.loads(m[0])",
      "newString": "    script = None\n    # strict=False: small local LLMs emit raw newlines/tabs inside JSON strings.\n    try:\n        script = json.loads(text, strict=False)\n    except Exception:\n        m = re.search(r\"\\{[\\s\\S]*\\}\", text)\n        if m:\n            script = json.loads(m[0], strict=False)",
      "allowMultiple": false
    }
  ]
}
```
